process_area.title: Responsible Sourcing Governance, Reporting & Stakeholder Engagement

value_stream.name: Human Rights, Modern Slavery & Responsible Supply Chain Due Diligence

fields.Participants: Sustainability, Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-122), Merchandising (links to VS-01), Legal (links to VS-100), HR (links to VS-19/VS-103), Compliance (links to VS-119), Finance (links to VS-17.4), Board (links to VS-36)

workflows.name: Responsible Sourcing Governance, Cross-Functional Steering & Decision Rights

Automation Opportunity: - System continuous audit of "operate the cross-functional responsible-sourcing steering" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "documented decision rights" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report governance effectiveness and material decisions to the Board Audit/Risk…" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-625 (ensure controlled execution — Responsible Sourcing Governance, Reporting & Stakeholder Engagement (PA-131.3).)
- operational: documented rights and Board oversight; operational: clear decision rights
Pain Points / Risks: - **Commercial-overrides risk**: Commercial pressure overriding human-rights decisions; mitigated by documented rights and Board oversight
- **Unclear-RACI risk**: Decisions stalled; mitigated by clear decision rights
System Touchpoints: - Governance (links to VS-36); procurement (links to VS-03/VS-122); ESG (links to VS-25); ethics (links to VS-119); audit (links to VS-21); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Sustainability/ESG Manager/VP Supply Chain operate the cross-functional responsible-sourcing steering: membership, cadence, decision rights (risk acceptance, sourcing consequences links to W4014, resource), escalation to CEO/Board, and integration with procurement, ESG (VS-25), ethics (VS-119), and audit (VS-21)

Sustainability/ESG Manager maintain the roles, RACI, and the policy/framework currency (links to W4001/W4003), and manage conflicts between commercial and human-rights priorities via documented decision rights
Sustainability/ESG Manager report governance effectiveness and material decisions to the Board Audit/Risk Committee (links to VS-36/VS-21.2)

fields.Participants: Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-67/VS-122), Sustainability, Global Sourcing (links to VS-122), Merchandising (links to VS-01), external trainers, affected suppliers
fields.Trigger: CAP findings (W4012); supplier-improvement need; strategic-vendor development

workflows.name: Supplier Development, Capacity Building & Incentive Program

Automation Opportunity: - System workflow orchestration of "coordinated with vendor scorecard development" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-measure of "measure program effectiveness" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-625 (ensure controlled execution — Responsible Sourcing Governance, Reporting & Stakeholder Engagement (PA-131.3).)
- operational: tailored programs; operational: meaningful commercial preference
Pain Points / Risks: - **One-size risk**: Generic training not addressing specific supplier gaps; mitigated by tailored programs
- **Incentive-ineffectiveness risk**: Incentives not changing behavior; mitigated by meaningful commercial preference
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/vendor (links to VS-03/VS-67/VS-122); merchandising (links to VS-01); analytics (links to VS-28); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Procurement/Sustainability design supplier development and capacity-building programs: training (labor standards, safety, responsible recruitment, management systems), toolkits, peer learning, and on-site coaching — coordinated with vendor scorecard development (links to VS-67.3)

Procurement build incentives: preferred-supplier status, volume preference, longer terms, co-investment, and recognition for strong human-rights performance; disincentives for non-compliance (links to W4014)
Procurement/Sustainability measure program effectiveness (supplier improvement, audit-score trends, CAP closure rates), and iterate (links to W4019)

fields.Participants: Sustainability, Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-67), Analytics (links to VS-28), Compliance (links to VS-119), Internal Audit (links to VS-21), CEO, Board

workflows.name: Human Rights KPI, Performance Management & Analytics

Automation Opportunity: - System continuous audit of "audit coverage and findings, CAP closure rate/time, grievance…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "review performance vs targets, identify laggards/systemic issues, and drive…" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report to the Board Audit/Risk Committee" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-625 (ensure controlled execution — Responsible Sourcing Governance, Reporting & Stakeholder Engagement (PA-131.3).)
- operational: outcome-oriented KPIs; operational: assurance and MDM (links to VS-29)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vanity-metric risk**: KPIs that don't reflect real impact; mitigated by outcome-oriented KPIs
- **Data-quality risk**: Incomplete/inaccurate supplier data; mitigated by assurance and MDM (links to VS-29)
System Touchpoints: - Analytics (links to VS-28); procurement/vendor (links to VS-03/VS-67); audit (links to VS-21); ESG (links to VS-25); governance (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: Sustainability/Analytics maintain human-rights KPIs: supplier risk-tier distribution, audit coverage and findings, CAP closure rate/time, grievance volume/substantiation, remediation outcomes, traceability coverage, living-wage progress, and program maturity
Sustainability/Procurement review performance vs targets, identify laggards/systemic issues, and drive improvement (links to W4018/W4012); integrate with vendor scorecard (links to VS-67)
Sustainability report to the Board Audit/Risk Committee (links to VS-36/VS-21.2) and into ESG reporting (links to VS-25.3/W4020)

fields.Participants: Sustainability, Legal (links to VS-100), Compliance, Procurement (links to VS-03), HR (links to VS-19), Finance (links to VS-17.4), Corporate Communications (links to VS-14.3), external assurance
fields.Trigger: Reporting cycle; B2B customer request; regulatory requirement

workflows.name: Modern Slavery / Human Rights Statutory & Voluntary Reporting

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "prepare statutory human-rights/modern-slavery disclosures where applicable" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-report of "Sustainability prepare voluntary disclosures integrated into ESG/sustainability reporting" (replaces manual Step 2).
Controls: - CTL-625 (ensure controlled execution — Responsible Sourcing Governance, Reporting & Stakeholder Engagement (PA-131.3).)
- operational: accuracy and external assurance; operational: reporting calendar and legal review; operational: statement not filed
Pain Points / Risks: - **Greenwashing risk**: Overstated progress; mitigated by accuracy and external assurance
- **Statutory-miss risk**: Required statement not filed; mitigated by reporting calendar and legal review
System Touchpoints: - ESG/reporting (links to VS-25.3); legal (links to VS-100); procurement (links to VS-03); HR (links to VS-19); comms (links to VS-14.3); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Sustainability/Legal prepare statutory human-rights/modern-slavery disclosures where applicable (modern-slavery statements for jurisdictions where BuildRight or its B2B customers operate — UK MSA, Australian MSA, German LkSG, EU CSDDD readiness) and respond to B2B-customer cascaded requests (questionnaires, CMRT/EMRT)

Sustainability prepare voluntary disclosures integrated into ESG/sustainability reporting (links to VS-25.3): UNGP progress, salient risks and actions, grievance/remediation data, KPIs, and goals — aligned to GRI/UNGC/SAI frameworks
Sustainability/Legal obtain external assurance where required, manage disclosure risk (greenwashing, sensitivity), publish, and respond to stakeholder queries (W4021)

fields.Participants: Sustainability, Legal (links to VS-100), Govt Affairs (links to VS-104), Corporate Communications (links to VS-14.3), Procurement (links to VS-03), HR, CEO
fields.Trigger: Material issue; stakeholder inquiry; strategic engagement

workflows.name: Human Rights Stakeholder, NGO & Investor Engagement

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-issue of "Sustainability/Comms engage stakeholders proactively and on material issues" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report engagement outcomes" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-625 (ensure controlled execution — Responsible Sourcing Governance, Reporting & Stakeholder Engagement (PA-131.3).)
- operational: proactive strategy; operational: clear positions and coordination
Pain Points / Risks: - **Reactive-only risk**: Engagement only on crisis; mitigated by proactive strategy
- **Position-incoherence risk**: Inconsistent messaging; mitigated by clear positions and coordination
System Touchpoints: - ESG/comms (links to VS-25/VS-14.3); govt affairs (links to VS-104); legal (links to VS-100); competition (links to VS-129); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Sustainability map human-rights stakeholders (NGOs, industry initiatives, investors/lenders, B2B customers, government, communities, workers) and develop an engagement strategy with clear positions and commitments

Sustainability/Comms engage stakeholders proactively and on material issues (allegations, findings, incidents), manage NGO/media engagement (links to VS-14.3 crisis-comms), and participate in industry/multi-stakeholder initiatives (links to VS-104.2 with competition guardrails)
Sustainability capture stakeholder input, feed into saliency (W4002) and program improvement (W4024), and report engagement outcomes (links to VS-25.3/W4020)

fields.Participants: HR (links to VS-19/VS-103/VS-102), Labor Relations (links to VS-84), Sustainability, Compliance (links to VS-119), Operations, contingent-workforce mgmt (links to VS-98)

workflows.name: Own-Operations Human Rights, DEI & Worker-Voice Integration

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-issue of "HR/Compliance operate own-operations worker voice and grievance" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "HR/Sustainability integrate own-operations findings into saliency" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-625 (ensure controlled execution — Responsible Sourcing Governance, Reporting & Stakeholder Engagement (PA-131.3).)
- operational: own-ops assessment; operational: contingent-workforce integration
Pain Points / Risks: - **Do-as-I-say risk**: Imposing standards on suppliers not met internally; mitigated by own-ops assessment
- **Contingent-blind-spot risk**: Non-employee conditions overlooked; mitigated by contingent-workforce integration
System Touchpoints: - HR/payroll (links to VS-19/VS-102/VS-103); labor relations (links to VS-84); HSE (links to VS-24); contingent workforce (links to VS-98); ethics (links to VS-119); ESG (links to VS-25)

steps.activity: HR/Sustainability assess BuildRight's own human-rights performance: labor standards (links to VS-19/VS-84), non-discrimination/DEI (links to VS-103.2), health & safety (links to VS-24), freedom of association (links to VS-84), living/competitive wage (links to VS-102), and contingent-workforce conditions (links to VS-98)
HR/Compliance operate own-operations worker voice and grievance (integrate with speak-up VS-119), ensure non-retaliation, and remediate own-operations issues
HR/Sustainability integrate own-operations findings into saliency (W4002) and reporting (W4020), ensuring BuildRight addresses its own impacts before imposing on suppliers

fields.Participants: Sustainability, L&D (links to VS-19.4), Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-122), Compliance (links to VS-119), HR (links to VS-103)
fields.Volume: Risk-role cohorts (Procurement, Merchandising, Global Sourcing, Audit, Compliance, executives)

workflows.name: Human Rights Training, Capability & Culture Program

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-track of "track completion with attestation" for the tiered human-rights training (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track completion with attestation" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-measure of "Sustainability reinforce culture" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-625 (ensure controlled execution — Responsible Sourcing Governance, Reporting & Stakeholder Engagement (PA-131.3).)
- operational: role scenarios and attestation; operational: risk-role register
Pain Points / Risks: - **Tick-box risk**: Training without behavior change; mitigated by role scenarios and attestation
- **Coverage-gap risk**: Risk roles missed; mitigated by risk-role register
System Touchpoints: - L&D/LMS (links to VS-19.4); ethics (links to VS-119); comms (links to VS-63/VS-103.1); HR (links to VS-103); records (links to VS-88)

steps.activity: Sustainability/L&D design tiered human-rights training: (a) all-employee awareness (code, speak-up, respect); (b) risk-role modules for Buyers/Merchandising/Global Sourcing (salient risks, sourcing decisions, vendor engagement) and Audit/Compliance (DD, remediation); (c) executive/board briefing
Sustainability/L&D deliver via LMS (links to VS-19.4), embed in role onboarding (links to VS-121/VS-123/VS-122), and track completion with attestation
Sustainability reinforce culture (comms links to VS-63/VS-103.1), refresh for findings/regulatory change, and measure effectiveness

fields.Participants: Sustainability, Legal (links to VS-100), Compliance, Procurement (links to VS-03/VS-122), Strategy (links to VS-33), Internal Audit (links to VS-21), CEO, Board
fields.Trigger: Annual program review; regulatory change; benchmark

workflows.name: Human Rights Program Maturity, Continuous Improvement & Emerging Regulation

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-monitor of "monitor emerging human-rights regulation" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "Sustainability/ESG Manager run the annual program maturity review" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-report of "report maturity and roadmap" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-625 (ensure controlled execution — Responsible Sourcing Governance, Reporting & Stakeholder Engagement (PA-131.3).)
- operational: monitoring and readiness assessment; operational: benchmarking and annual review
Pain Points / Risks: - **Regulatory-lag risk**: New requirements unaddressed; mitigated by monitoring and readiness assessment
- **Maturity-stagnation risk**: Program not improving; mitigated by benchmarking and annual review
System Touchpoints: - Strategy (links to VS-33); legal/compliance (links to VS-100/VS-119); procurement (links to VS-03/VS-122); audit (links to VS-21); ESG (links to VS-25); governance (links to VS-36)

steps.activity: Sustainability/ESG Manager/Legal monitor emerging human-rights regulation (EU CSDDD, German LkSG, US UFLPA, UK/Australian MSA, PH developments) and B2B-customer/regulator expectations, and assess BuildRight's exposure and readiness
Sustainability/ESG Manager run the annual program maturity review (against UNGP/ISO frameworks and peers), identify gaps, benchmark, and prioritize improvements (process, data, scope, geographies)
Sustainability/ESG Manager/CEO secure budget/resources from the Board (links to VS-36), iterate the strategy (links to W4001/W4003), and report maturity and roadmap
